A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COMMA benchmark and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. The appendices match in both extracted text and rendered pages, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original model and human evaluations on ten puzzles, failure analyses, and memory and single-agent ablations in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains original benchmark results, failure analyses, the memory ablation, and additional experimental statistics in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The Solver–Expert framework, information allocation, memory architecture, interaction procedure, and Appendix D prompts remain unchanged. Removing an evaluated single-agent control does not revise the proposed framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten puzzles across four capability categories, including the same PAD-UFES-20-based telehealth task. The removed single-agent experiment is an information-access control within these retained tasks.

E2.justification: v5 removes the full-information GPT-4o Single Agent comparator from Table 2. The model, human, and random comparator sets in Table 1 and Appendix C remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 drops the control giving one agent both the puzzle image and solution manual, leaving the full-memory versus no-memory comparison. The retained experiments keep the same stated sampling, conversation limits, mistake limits, decoding settings, and metrics.

E4.justification: The single-agent/view-asymmetry ablation is removed from Section 5.3 and Table 2 without relocation to an appendix. The memory ablation, failure cases, conversation-length analysis, privacy analysis, and efficiency analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same stated independent-run counts and standard-error reporting, including the 100/30/10 counts by agent type in Table 1. Removing the Single Agent row removes associated uncertainty values but does not change statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: v5 deletes the Single Agent results from Table 2, including its 40.41 ± 1.4% overall partial success rate and ten per-puzzle scores. The retained full-memory and no-memory scores, Table 1 results, plotted findings, and Appendix C results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The efficiency-score definition in Equation 1 and other metric definitions retain their mathematical meaning. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about the communication benchmark, weaknesses of evaluated models, and privacy failures. The removed ablation does not produce a corresponding revision to these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets Table 2 as showing that collaboration helps some puzzles while individual reasoning better handles others, citing LED and Color. v5 removes this task-dependent qualification and discusses only memory benefits. Other interpretations and Section 7 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The memory-ablation description now explicitly restricts each agent to the latest message, where v3 referred generically to the agent. This modest clarification does not establish a procedural change. Hardware, decoding parameters, model versions, prompts, and the code/data link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged, including the related-work discussion and the benchmark's relationship to existing agent evaluations. The added NSF funding acknowledgement is not a related-work addition.

P1.justification: v5 expands and updates author affiliations and contact details, adds NSF acknowledgement text, shortens several passages, and renames the ablation discussion to Effect of Conversation Memory. The broader section organization and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The expanded author block shifts the introduction and subsequent pagination. Figure 4 moves from page 9 to page 10, Figure 5's caption is shortened, and Table 2 loses a row and receives a revised caption. Appendix displays remain identical.

improvement.justification: Removing the full-information single-agent control and its task-dependent interpretation weakens readers' ability to assess when collaboration helps on this communication-focused benchmark. The small documentation and presentation refinements do not compensate for that loss of relevant evidence. The decline is limited because the main results, remaining analyses, and appendices are preserved.
